rag.description: The InvokeDataForEachLoop plugin iterates over the records of a JSON or XML data payload and runs a set of child rules once per record. Before each iteration it injects the current record's values into the child rules through {{$ --Field}}, {{$ --Path}}, and {{$ --Item}} tokens, enabling data-driven RPA and automated testing without scripting each step manually.

qa.question: What is the InvokeDataForEachLoop plugin?
qa.answer: It is an automation action that parses a JSON or XML payload into records and runs a series of child rules on each record in sequence, injecting the record's values into those rules first.

qa.question: How is InvokeDataForEachLoop different from InvokeForEachLoop?
qa.answer: InvokeForEachLoop iterates over DOM elements found by a locator, while InvokeDataForEachLoop iterates over data records parsed from a JSON or XML payload.

qa.question: Where does the data payload come from?
qa.answer: When the Base64 switch is absent the payload is taken from Argument as raw content or a file path; when Base64 is present the payload is taken from the DataSource parameter and decoded from Base64.

qa.question: Which data formats are supported?
qa.answer: JSON and XML. The format is auto-detected (JSON first, then XML) and the action throws when the content is neither valid JSON nor valid XML.

qa.question: What happens when a single object is provided instead of an array?
qa.answer: A single JSON object or value, or a non-repeating XML root, is wrapped into a one-item collection and iterated exactly once.

qa.question: How does the plugin identify records in XML?
qa.answer: Repeated same-named child elements of the root are treated as an array of records; any other root shape is treated as a single object and wrapped as one record.

qa.question: How do I read a field of the current record inside a child rule?
qa.answer: Use the token {{$ --Field:name }}, which resolves to the named JSON member or the matching XML child element (then attribute) of the current record.

qa.question: How do I read a nested value from the current record?
qa.answer: Use {{$ --Path:expr }}, which evaluates a JSONPath expression for JSON records and an XPath expression for XML records.

qa.question: How do I inject the whole current record?
qa.answer: Use {{$ --Item }}, which injects the current record as a string: minified JSON or XML for complex records, or the scalar text for a simple-array value.

qa.question: What happens if a token cannot be resolved?
qa.answer: A missing field or unmatched path leaves the token unchanged so a nested InvokeDataForEachLoop can resolve it against its own record, while a field that exists but resolves to null or throws yields an empty string.

qa.question: Can InvokeDataForEachLoop be nested?
qa.answer: Yes. Because unresolved tokens are kept as-is, an outer loop injects only the values it owns and a nested loop resolves its own tokens against its own records.

qa.question: Who authored the InvokeDataForEachLoop plugin?
qa.answer: The plugin was authored by Roei Sabag.

description: ### Purpose

Iterates over the records of a JSON or XML payload and runs a set of child rules on each record. Before every iteration the current record's values are injected into the child rules through `{{$ --Field}}`, `{{$ --Path}}`, and `{{$ --Item}}` tokens. It supports nested loops for multi-level, data-driven workflows, making it easier to automate repetitive tasks in RPA and automated testing.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature              | Description                                                                     |
| Record Iteration     | Parses a JSON or XML payload into records and loops through each one.            |
| Value Injection      | Replaces `--Field`, `--Path`, and `--Item` tokens with the current record data. |
| Format Auto-Detection| Detects JSON or XML automatically and throws when the content matches neither.   |
| Nested Loop Capability| Allows data loops inside loops, each resolving its own tokens per record.       |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case            | Description                                                                       |
| Data Processing     | Process each record in a JSON or XML result by running data entry or validation.  |
| Batch Operations    | Perform a series of tasks on each item returned from a script or an API response. |
| Data-Driven Flows   | Drive downstream rules with values taken from each record in turn.                |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case               | Description                                                                 |
| Data-Driven Testing    | Run the same steps across every record in a data set.                       |
| Fixture Expansion      | Expand a single object or a small array into repeated, parameterized steps. |
| Result Verification    | Verify downstream behavior for each record produced by a previous action.   |

annotations.expected_result: For each object in the array, a RegisterParameter rule runs with the record's `firstName` value injected into its argument.
annotations.notes: InvokeDataForEachLoop parses the JSON array into two records and runs the child RegisterParameter once per record. The `{{$ --Field:firstName}}` token is replaced with the current record's `firstName` value before the child rule executes.

description: ### Iterate JSON Objects And Inject A Field
Iterates over each object in the JSON array supplied through the argument and runs a RegisterParameter action for each one.
The child rule uses `{{$ --Field:firstName}}` to inject the current record's `firstName` value into its argument before it runs.
If a record is missing the `firstName` field, the token is kept as-is for the child rule to handle.

annotations.expected_result: For each record, a RegisterParameter rule runs with the nested `user.email` value injected via JSONPath.
annotations.notes: InvokeDataForEachLoop parses the JSON array into records and resolves `{{$ --Path:$.user.email}}` as a JSONPath expression against each record, injecting the nested email into the child rule.

description: ### Iterate JSON Objects And Inject A Nested Value With JSONPath
Iterates over each object in the JSON array and runs a RegisterParameter action for each one.
The child rule uses `{{$ --Path:$.user.email}}` to resolve the nested `user.email` value from the current record via JSONPath.
If the path matches no node, the token is kept as-is so a nested data loop can resolve it later.

annotations.expected_result: For each value in the simple array, a WriteLog rule logs the current item.
annotations.notes: InvokeDataForEachLoop iterates over a simple JSON array of strings and injects each value through `{{$ --Item}}`, which resolves to the scalar text of the current record.

description: ### Iterate A Simple Array And Inject Each Item
Iterates over each value in the simple JSON string array and runs a WriteLog action for each one.
The child rule uses `{{$ --Item}}` to inject the current value, which resolves to the scalar text of a simple-array record.
Complex records injected through `{{$ --Item}}` are emitted as minified JSON or XML instead.

annotations.expected_result: For each `<user>` element, a RegisterParameter rule runs with the record's `name` element value injected into its argument.
annotations.notes: InvokeDataForEachLoop treats the repeated same-named `<user>` elements as an array of records and resolves `{{$ --Field:name}}` as the matching XML child element of each record.

description: ### Iterate XML Records And Inject A Child Element
Parses the XML payload and iterates over each repeated `<user>` element as a record, running a RegisterParameter action for each one.
The child rule uses `{{$ --Field:name}}` to inject the current record's `name` child element value before it runs.
A non-repeating XML root is instead treated as a single record and iterated exactly once.

annotations.expected_result: The Base64 DataSource is decoded to a JSON array, and a RegisterParameter rule runs for each record with the `name` value injected.
annotations.notes: With the Base64 switch present, InvokeDataForEachLoop reads the DataSource parameter, decodes it from Base64 into `[{"name":"Alice"},{"name":"Bob"}]`, and iterates the resulting records. An invalid Base64 value throws.

description: ### Iterate A Base64-Encoded Payload From DataSource
Reads the payload from the `DataSource` parameter and decodes it from Base64 because the `Base64` switch is present.
The decoded JSON array is iterated, and the child RegisterParameter action injects each record's `name` value through `{{$ --Field:name}}`.
When `Base64` is present and the value is not valid Base64, the action throws.

annotations.expected_result: The single JSON object is wrapped into a one-item collection, and a WriteLog rule runs once with the `name` value injected.
annotations.notes: InvokeDataForEachLoop wraps a single JSON object into a one-item array and iterates exactly once, resolving `{{$ --Field:name}}` against that single record.

description: ### Iterate A Single Object By Wrapping It Into One Record
Accepts a single JSON object and wraps it into a one-item collection so the child rules run exactly once.
The child WriteLog action uses `{{$ --Field:name}}` to inject the object's `name` value.
This tolerance keeps passing a lone object simple when data comes from a script result.
The JSON or XML payload to iterate, used only when the `Base64` switch is present.
Accepts a raw Base64 value or a file path whose contents are Base64; the value is decoded from Base64 before parsing.
An invalid Base64 value throws and stops the action.
parameters.name: DataSource

description: Reads the payload from `DataSource` and decodes it from Base64 before parsing and iterating.
When omitted, the payload is taken from `Argument` as raw content or a file path.
Throws when the resolved value is not valid Base64.
parameters.name: Base64

description: Provides the JSON or XML payload to iterate when the `Base64` switch is absent, as raw content or a file path.
Supersedes `DataSource`, which is only used in Base64 mode.
properties.name: Argument

description: The set of child rules to run once per record.
Before each record, the `{{$ --Field}}`, `{{$ --Path}}`, and `{{$ --Item}}` tokens inside these rules are replaced with values from the current record.
properties.name: Rules

summary: Iterates over the records of a JSON or XML payload and runs child rules on each one sequentially.
Injects each record's values into the child rules through `--Field`, `--Path`, and `--Item` tokens.
Supports Base64-encoded input, single-object normalization, and nested data loops.
